title: A Thermal-Time Framework for S₁ Progenies of Medicinal Cannabis sativa L. under Tropical Conditions: Conserved Phenological Thresholds and Genotype-Specific Biomass Allocation
content: Medicinal Cannabis sativa L. is expanding into tropical regions, but agronomic reference values derive from temperate or indoor environments. We evaluated thermal requirements, biomass partitioning, and morphometric predictors in three medicinal cannabis S1 progenies under tropical conditions. Purple Wreck (THC-dominant), Doctor (CBD-dominant), and Schanti (balanced) were grown under a 20-h photoperiod during vegetative growth and then transferred outdoors under natural photoperiod. Organ dry biomass was sampled weekly and modeled against growing degree days (GDD) using three-parameter log-logistic functions. Thermal positioning did not differ detectably among progenies, whereas asymptotic biomass differed, indicating variation in biomass magnitude and reproductive allocation rather than developmental timing. Pooled thresholds occurred at 871 GDD for onset of active vegetative growth, 1329 GDD for stem elongation, 1425 GDD for flowering onset, 1543 GDD for onset of active floral biomass accumulation, and 1947 GDD for inflorescence formation. Harvest index was projected to stabilize at ~2263 GDD and onset of inflorescence maturation at ~2457 GDD, both beyond the sampled window. At a common developmental stage, morphometric descriptors added little to thermal time, although crown diameter showed the strongest within-stage association with floral biomass (r = 0.31). Thermal time reliably described growth and reproductive allocation once floral induction was photoperiodically permitted.
